full_judgment: 16. It appears from the record that prosecution examined only one independent witness who happens to be PW 7 and has been declared hostile by the prosecution. The learned Assistant Sessions Judge did not consider his evidence on the fact that he has been declared hostile. The evidence of only private non-interested witness (PW 7) should not be thrown out of consideration lightly. He has been declared hostile by the prosecution. Such evidence is not necessarily untrue and cannot be treated by court as unworthy of credit unless the prosecution proves by way of cross of such witness that he (PW 7) due to hostile animus is not willing to speak the truth. Record shows nothing could be elicited from him as to why he could tell lie or throw doubt in his evidence. It is highly improbable that a neighbour will tell lie with whom the informant or any member of his house has got any enmity with him(PW 7) Lastly non-examination of independent witness, particularly some of the neighbours raises presumption against the prosecution of the effect that had they been examined they would not have supported the case of the prosecution. The defence is not obliged to prove its case. A criminal Court is to consider whether the prosecution by its evidence could establish its own case and the court is not to give stress on the defence case. The defence would discharge its burden if from such circumstances a reasonable doubt could be created. In the present case prosecution totally failed to prove its case required under law. The submissions of the learned Advocate for the appellant is thus found to have substance.
